claims.text: A staged solution-and-aging treatment will improve ductility and uniform deformability in a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The treatment will preserve or increase the alloy's high strength.
The treatment will preserve impact-induced energy release.
The untreated alloy has a coarse precipitate structure.
The untreated alloy has a primarily BCC matrix.
Solution treatment at about 1100 °C followed by aging at 700–800 °C will induce uniformly distributed coherent nanoscale precipitates.
The proposed mechanical-property benefit should hold at ambient conditions.
The proposed benefit should also hold under high-strain-rate or impact loading.
Uniform coherent nanoprecipitates will be embedded in the primary refractory BCC matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby preserve high strength.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate controlled dislocation transmission and interfacial stress relaxation.
The precipitates minimize localized stress concentrations during dynamic high-strain events.
Nanoprecipitation can delay localized plastic instability and promote more uniform deformation.
Untreated tungsten-based refractory HEAs have high strength but limited ductility and non-uniform deformation under high-strain-rate impact.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treated alloy will have greater uniform elongation and less strain localization.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treated alloy will retain or slightly increase tensile strength.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the treated alloy will deliver similar impact-induced energy release.
Precise treatment control is required to avoid precipitate coarsening or brittle secondary-phase formation and obtain the proposed strength-ductility synergy.
The magnitude of improvement depends on processing conditions and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that improperly controlled processing and resulting coarsening may simply fail to create the required mediator, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of non-uniform or coarsened precipitates as falsification of the causal hypothesis. Failure to implement the stipulated microstructure would not by itself falsify the effect of that microstructure.
